subject: Velociti pilot: request for trial extension + combined credits & enterprise discount
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily@velociti.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot delays — request for trial extension + credits

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looks promising and our ML team is excited to run the full ingestion. We hit a snag on our side: procurement has pushed our contract review out by at least six weeks due to a security questionnaire and a new budget cycle. That means our current 30‑day pilot window won't be enough to prove value.

Before we escalate internally I wanted to check if Redwood can offer (a) a 90‑day trial extension, (b) supplemental credits to cover the next month of usage (~$10k), and (c) a one‑time enterprise discount on the first year (15%) if we sign a committed pilot/PO once procurement clears. Our exec sponsor (CFO) is watching spend closely; if we can show a bit more runway and a price concession, we can get a fast path through procurement once paperwork clears.

Appreciate a frank read — if you can route this to your side for approval it would help our timeline significantly.

Attached: current pilot report (small) and timelines.zip (references).

Best,
Emily Park
Director, Data Science
Velociti Inc.
emily@velociti.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@velociti.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot delays — request for trial extension + credits

Hi Emily — thanks for the note and for flagging procurement timing. Totally understand the need for more runway to finish the evaluation.

I can take this to our commercial approvals forum, but to set expectations up front: larger extensions and credit packages require exec signoff because they affect reserved capacity economics. Tentative offer I will ask for on your behalf:
- Pilot extension: +60 days (total 90 days)
- Supplemental credits: $8,000 applied to pilot usage
- Introductory enterprise discount: 10% on year‑one committed spend (conditional on signed PO/commit within 45 days after procurement clearance)

If you can share the procurement timeline and confirm the expected committed spend range, that will help the approval case (we escalate differently for $75k+ vs $200k+ ARR potential). I attached a draft SOW that maps the proposed extension and deliverables.

I loop Ben (sales lead) here to vet commercial terms; I’ll also route to Marissa for exec approval. I’ll come back to you by EOD Wednesday with a final update.

Attachment: Velociti_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 230 KB)

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot delays — request for trial extension + credits — exec approval request

Ben / Marissa,

Forwarding Velociti's ask — summary and recommendation below. They are a mid‑market logistics analytics shop; strong ML team, clear use case for our retrieval/embedding features. Why I think we should approve (with limits):
- Ask: 90‑day extension, $10k supplemental credits, 15% first‑year discount (their procurement pushed timeline out 6+ weeks)
- Recommendation: Approve a middle ground to keep momentum — extended runway to eliminate the timing risk but protect our economics: 75 additional days (so total pilot 105 days), $9,000 credits, 10% discount on year‑one with a performance clause (commit to $100k ARR within 6 months or discount recouped).
- Commercial rationale: Pipeline shows potential for $150k ARR (probability ~40%). Cost of the credit/extension is outweighed by expected CLTV if we convert.
- Risks: If procurement stalls beyond 90 days we eat support/compute without conversion; if they sign a smaller deal (<$50k) the concession is heavy.

Attachments: Velociti_SOW_v1.pdf (included), HubSpot deal VEL-2027-0042.

Request: Marissa — can you sign off on the above conditional package or advise adjustments? Fast approval helps close before their Q2 budget window.

Thanks,
Soojin
Account Executive
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot delays — request for trial extension + credits — exec approval request

Thanks for the clear summary, Soojin. I appreciate the pipeline context — Velociti looks like a good fit but we need measurable guardrails on the concession. I approve a conditional package with these edits: 

Approved terms (conditional):
- Pilot extension: +75 days (new pilot end = original end + 75 days)
- Supplemental credits: $9,000 (applied pro rata to pilot usage)
- Introductory enterprise discount: 10% on year‑one committed spend, valid only if Velociti executes a signed PO/contract within 60 days after pilot completion and the first‑year ARR is >= $100,000. If the $100k threshold is not met, we reserve the right to revoke the discount and invoice the difference.

Operational asks before commitment: 1) Update and send the SOW with these terms to Velociti (include performance clause language), 2) Secure a procurement point of contact and expected PO date, 3) Capture the commitment/forecast in HubSpot (deal VEL-2027-0042) and attach signed SOW to the record.

Soojin — please communicate these conditional terms to Emily and get a written acknowledgement from their procurement contact (procurement@velociti.com). Once we have that, route the updated SOW to Legal for a quick DocuSign (Icc: legal for FYI).

Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
